page: Amazon Web Services r5n.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Performance benchmarks show a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, falling into the bottom 25% in stress-ng and Geekbench tests. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently rank in the average tier. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 7004.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 14138.82. Memory read bandwidth reaches 87.18 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 13.18 million operations per second.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded capabilities, the r5n.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring significant memory capacity without demanding top-tier single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, and medium-scale data processing tasks.
